column1: # The answer key for matrix/run_matrix.sh. Checked by matrix/verify_matrix.mjs.
# run_matrix.sh records exit codes into a table and then exits 0 whatever those codes
# were. It is a recorder, not a check. So a CI job that runs it and reads $? proves only
# that the harness did not crash, which is the same defect the matrix exists to document:
# a check whose expected value comes from the thing it is checking.
# This file is the independent expectation. It is a literal, the way
# InterstitialCadenceTest's CUE_AFTER_RUN is a literal instead of being derived from
# INTERSTITIAL_EVERY. Nothing generates it. If a cell below disagrees with a real run,
# one of three things is true and all three need a human:
#   1. a check regressed and stopped firing,
#   2. a check improved and started firing, or
#   3. docs/field-note-fault-matrix.md and the published article are now wrong.
# The cells are the re-run table in docs/field-note-fault-matrix.md ("The re-run"), the
# state after 2b2bfb7 fixed the two blindnesses the first run found. The first-run table
# in that same note is history and is NOT what this key pins: it had F3 U=pass.
# Columns, per run_matrix.sh:
#   S  GameEngineTest.theSameSeedProducesTheSameRun   same-runtime determinism
#   G  ParityTraceTest                               golden file
#   D  node compare_trace.mjs over the TeaVM artifact differential
#   U  InterstitialCadenceTest                       the cadence unit test (footnote column)
# Why each row reads the way it does:
#   baseline  nothing injected, so every check must be green. This row is the only one
#             that proves the harness can report a pass at all.
#   F1        caught ONLY by D. S compares the JVM to itself and the golden file's JVM
#             side never moves, so neither can see the runtimes disagree.
#   F2        caught ONLY by G. Both builds compile the moved constant, so they move
#             together and D sees agreement.
#   F3        caught ONLY by U, and only since 2b2bfb7. G and D stay green on purpose:
#             the scripted run dies once, so runsSinceInterstitial reads 0 then 1 and
#             never approaches any threshold. Recording a field is not covering a
#             behaviour, and this row is the evidence for that sentence.
# S is pass on all four rows. That column cannot distinguish anything, which is the
# finding, not a gap in the key. It stays here so that an S that ever goes red is loud.
# ERROR is not a legal value in this file. ERROR is run_matrix.sh's word for "the harness
# broke" (exit 3, a failed build or a dead node step), and a key that could accept it
# would let a broken harness satisfy the gate. verify_matrix.mjs rejects it on both sides.
# Whitespace-separated, five fields per row. Add a row here when you add a patch to
# matrix/faults/ and a case to run_matrix.sh; the verifier cross-checks this file against
# the patches on disk, so a patch with no row and a row with no patch both go red.
case
baseline
F1_runtime_supplied_rng
F2_shared_constant
F3_untraced_cadence
